pageCache.pageTitle: Berry Hill Primary School - Home Page
pageCache.text:
We currently have spaces in Year 2 and Year 4
I am delighted to extend a very warm welcome to you and your child to Berry Hill Primary School on behalf of the children, staff, parents, and Governors. Since joining in January 2023, I have taken great pride in serving as the Headteacher of our wonderful school.
At Berry Hill, we are dedicated to providing the best opportunities and outcomes for every child. We recognise and celebrate the unique qualities of each individual child and strive to help them achieve their full academic potential while ensuring their health and happiness are nurtured.
Situated in the heart of Berry Hill, Coleford, our single-form village primary school is an integral part of the community. Collaboration with parents, carers, and the wider community is highly valued as we work together to support our children's development and growth.
Our school boasts an impressive range of facilities, including a vast field with a dedicated forest schools area, a library, a computer room and Buddies (our before and after-school club). These resources provide enriching experiences and support our holistic approach to education.
With our vision The Berry Hill Family - Valued individuals, aspirational learners, exceptional futures - we are committed to creating a caring and nurturing environment where every child can flourish academically and personally.
I encourage you to explore our website to gain insight into our school community. However, nothing compares to experiencing our school firsthand. I warmly invite you to visit us to see the vibrant learning environment we have created at Berry Hill.
Should you have any queries or wish to learn more about our school, please feel free to contact us. We eagerly anticipate the opportunity to connect with you and welcome you into our Berry Hill family.
Mrs Amy PughHeadteacher
What do our parents say about Berry Hill Primary School?
“You are not only supportive of the children but for the parents as well, and any concerns I have ever had, which haven’t been many have been answered. It’s a very good School, in my opinion”
“The school has a lovely community feel where the children are met with fantastic staff who put so much effort into their roles. All staff I have met have been so friendly and welcoming, I feel 100% confident that my child is receiving the best care and education at Berry Hill.”
“Having Pastoral support is great when needed. It has been great with my child’s transition of coming into a new class.”
“At the most recent parent evening, I was pleased to be able to see my child’s school books so examples of his work could be discussed when I met with his teacher. This shows my feedback is valued as in the last survey; I commented how as a full-time working parent, I have previously been unable to see my child’s work as books were not out at previous parents’ evenings, only at families in school days.”
“There is now so much more on offer for children at playtimes which my child talks about very positively. It has also been wonderful to see all the extracurricular provisions in place for the children, sporting events and the upcoming Young Voices concert in February. The list goes on as there are many improvements to the school.”
“Parent engagement, it's nice to always be able to chat on pick up and not feel rushed or like a burden. Each teacher my child has had takes the time to answer any questions.”
“The pairing of the year 5 children with reception buddies is fantastic. It helped support my child when he was in reception, and it has been even more wonderful for him now that he is in year 5. It seems to bring a lovely caring and nurturing side in the year 5 children.”
“The school seems fun by having after-school clubs, OPAL and events, like the PTA planned events and Christmas nativity etc.”

pageCache.text:
School Dinner Menu - £2.85 a day
BHPS Autumn 1 Dinner Menu 26-27
BHPS Autumn 2 & Spring 1 Dinner Menu 26-27
Children may choose to eat a school dinner cooked on the premises or bring a packed lunch from home.
School dinners cost £2.85 a day and we ask that you pay in advance via Parent Pay.
Packed LunchIf you prefer your child to bring a packed lunch, please ensure this does not contain nuts, sweets, gum or glass containers. Chocolate biscuits are allowed as part of the packed lunch.
Universal Free School MealsReception, Year 1 and Year 2 are entitled to Universal Free School Meals (which every child gets regardless of income or circumstances).
Free School MealsYour child may be entitled to Free School Meals. Please visit the GCC website to see more information and to apply.
SnackAt break times, our infant children have free fruit provided under the DFE initiative; pupils can bring their healthy snacks from home if they prefer. Crips, chocolate, sweets and highly sugared confectionery bars are not permitted at break time.
Year 3 to Year 6 can buy bread sticks, rice cakes or on some days piece of toast or fruit for 20p a day or they can bring a piece of fruit or vegetable from home.
Under the CoolMilk scheme, milk (ordered online by parents/carers) is provided free of charge to pupils under 5 years and at a cost to the remainder of the school.
Children are also encouraged to drink their own drink at break time, ensuring that they return to the classroom prepared and refreshed for learning.
MilkOur school takes part in the school milk scheme. If you want your child to have milk at school, please register at coolmilk.com. Milk is available free of charge to all children up to the age of 5. If you would like your child to continue receiving milk after they turn 5, a small fee applies.
Healthy Lunchbox Tips
Click >HERE< for healthy lunchbox tips
Keep them fuller for longer
Base the main lunchbox item on foods like bread, rice, pasta and potatoes. Choose wholegrain where you can.
Freeze for variety
Keep a small selection of different types of bread in the freezer so you have a variety of options – like bagels, pittas and wraps, granary, wholemeal and multigrain.
DIY lunches
Wraps and pots of fillings can be more exciting for kids when they get to make them. Dipping foods are also fun and a nice change from a sandwich each day.
Cut back on fat
Pick lower-fat fillings – like lean meats (including chicken or turkey), fish (such as tuna or salmon), lower-fat spread, reduced-fat cream cheese and reduced-fat hard cheese. And try to avoid using mayonnaise in sandwiches.
See more healthier swap ideas
Mix your slices
If your child does not like wholegrain, try making a sandwich from 1 slice of white bread and 1 slice of brown bread.
Always add veg
Cherry tomatoes, or sticks of carrot, cucumber, celery and peppers all count towards their 5 A Day. Adding a small pot of reduced-fat hummus or other dips may help with getting kids to eat vegetables.
Ever green
Always add salad to sandwiches and wraps too – it all counts towards your child's 5 A Day!
Cheesy does it…
Cheese can be high in fat and salt, so choose stronger-tasting ones – and use less of it – or try reduced-fat varieties.
Cut down on crisps
If your child really likes their crisps try reducing the number of times you include them in their lunchbox, and swap for homemade plain popcorn or plain rice cakes instead.
Add bite-sized fruit
Try chopped apple, peeled satsuma segments, strawberries, blueberries, halved grapes or melon slices to make it easier for them to eat. Add a squeeze of lemon juice to stop it from going brown.
Tinned fruit counts too
A small pot of tinned fruit in juice – not syrup – is perfect for a lunchbox and easily stored in the cupboard.
Swap the fruit bars
Dried fruit like raisins, sultanas and dried apricots are not only cheaper than processed fruit bars and snacks but can be healthier too. Just remember to keep dried fruit to mealtimes as it can be bad for teeth.
Switch the sweets
Swap cakes, chocolate, cereal bars and biscuits for malt loaf, fruited teacakes, fruit breads or fruit (fresh, dried or tinned – in juice not syrup).
Yoghurts: go low-fat and lower-sugar
Pop in low-fat and lower-sugar yoghurts or fromage frais and add your own fruit.
Get them involved
Get your kids involved in preparing and choosing what goes in their lunchbox. They are more likely to eat it if they helped make it.
Variety is the spice of lunch!
Be adventurous and get creative to mix up what goes in their lunchbox. Keeping them guessing with healthier ideas will keep them interested and more open to trying things.
Plan to Eatwell
The guide shows how much of what we eat overall should come from each food group to achieve a healthy, balanced diet. It can be really useful when thinking about what goes into kids' lunchboxes.
